body:
```suggestion
			bool remote_use_thread = !GDScriptLanguageServer::use_stdio && (bool)_EDITOR_GET("network/language_server/use_thread");
```
Let's not use ternaries like this, it has horrible readability
Putting the `read != 1` condition here seems wrong to me. Other errors might return read=0, and should not be interpreted as `ERR_BUSY`.
I assume there is a reason for using `OS::get_singleton()->print` over `print_line` or `EditorNode::get_log()->add_message`?

If I use `EditorNode` those messages doesn't end up on the stdout, so I searched the code trying to find the "correct" way to print to stdout. I ended up finding `OS::get_singleton()->print` but sadly I didn't notice `print_line`. Changing it to use it.
It probably should check if handles are `-1` and set some error flag to avoid IO calls with invalid handles.
I assume it's only useful when `stdio` is pipe, so probably can reuse `get_length` from `FileAccessWindowsPipe`/`FileAccessUnixPipe` to get actual value.
